transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-07T16:00:00-07:00
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Eng); Jordan Lee (LumenFleet Eng), Maya Singh (PM), Omar Patel (SRE)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync. SDK usage questions, function-calling schema drift, a few reproducible cases where structured output fails validation on longer prompts.

00:00 Alex: okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call?
00:06 Jordan: hey Alex, Jordan here.
00:08 Maya: Maya—PM.
00:09 Omar: Omar on SRE.
00:11 Priya: Priya here from Redwood, SE.
00:13 Diego: Diego on infra.
00:15 Alex: cool. Today we want to go over the JSON schema failures you flagged, some SDK wiring notes, and the proposed tuning for batching / kv cache.

02:35 Jordan: Yeah so we ran the latest SDK integration in staging, using the node-sdk default client. Everything wired fine for simple tool calls, but when the system prompt plus chat history approaches 6k tokens we start seeing malformed structured outputs—missing commas, stray quotes, sometimes keys renamed to similar words. It's intermittent.
02:58 Priya: got it. that's a known surface area — model variants + sampling temp sometimes interact with the function-calling wrappers. can you paste a small example?
03:10 Jordan: uh sure I dropped one into the shared doc — response id sf-113. Example: expected {"route":"A12","eta_minutes":12} but got {route:"A12" eta_minutes":12} which breaks our json.parse.
03:29 Diego: that looks like a keypad of punctuation collapse in the tokenization phase. also curious — which model/variant were you hitting in the call?
03:38 Jordan: we pinned to redwood-model-1.3-raw for parity with prod. tokens per call peaked ~9k including history during the run.
03:49 Priya: two immediate levers: 1) move to the function-calling strict mode via the SDK (we have a flag in 0.8.2) that enforces structured-output patterns, 2) post-response sanitizer that repairs common punctuation issues before parse. both are quick wins.

06:10 Maya: is strict mode guaranteed? we can't have subtle changes to content. our downstream pipeline assumes exact schema.
06:18 Priya: not 100% guaranteed—strict mode biases decoding toward schema tokens and reduces hallucinated keys, but it's still probabilistic. Think of it as greatly lowered error rate, not absolute. For absolute enforcement we recommend two-stage: function-calling plus a validation+retry loop. If validation fails, call the model again with the exact failure case as context and a stronger temperature 0.0.
06:45 Alex: we sometimes suggest adding an explicit wrapper token like <JSON_START> ... <JSON_END> to reduce stray text. you might also use deterministic sampling for critical routes.

09:12 Omar: from SRE side, any impact to latency with those retries and stricter decode? we're tight on 95th percentile.
09:22 Priya: retries obviously add latency on failure paths. typical strict-mode overhead is negligible at single-call decode but if you do validation+retry worst-case adds one extra model invocation. Instead, we recommend prefix-caching: store validated prefixes in KV cache so that repeated prefixes hit cached continuations and you avoid full decode on frequent flows.
09:50 Diego: batching also helps with cost but may increase tail latency. for LumenFleet's peak qps we suggested a small batch size (b=4) with a 15ms wait window as a compromise. That keeps median low but controls cost.

12:40 Jordan: quick question on SDK wiring — we saw two ways to attach the function handlers: the high-level declarative registerFunction call vs the raw callback mapping. which do you recommend?
12:52 Priya: registerFunction is simpler and plays nicely with our function-calling enforcement; the callback mapping gives you lower-level control for streaming partial outputs. If you need partial updates in UI we can show how to combine both.
13:12 Alex: and don't forget the offline validator we shipped — it's a small node script that runs a batch of responses through ajv schema checks and reports fail rates. helps you quantify progress.

16:05 Maya: we ran the offline validator and saw a 2.7% fail rate on the weekend run, but the failures cluster around longer contexts and occasional numerical formatting (e.g., 12.0 vs 12).
16:24 Priya: numeric normalization is common. we usually normalize on the client: cast numeric-like strings to ints and fail the schema only if it doesn't coerce cleanly. also lower temperature and enforce eos tokens.

18:50 Jordan: can Redwood produce an example minimal repo that demonstrates strict mode + validator + retry? I want the engineers to run it in our CI quickly.
18:58 Alex: yes we can. Alex to share example repo and a trimmed README by Friday.
19:05 Jordan: sweet. also security — Omar flagged KMS integration for token encryption in private deployment. what's the ask from Redwood?
19:18 Priya: for Private you can point the Redwood agent at your KMS/HSM; we support AWS KMS and Google KMS out of the box and HSM via PKCS11 adapter. For hosted accounts we offer customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. We will share the security pack.
19:45 Omar: and audit logs? we need per-request metadata for compliance.
19:51 Diego: Console can export per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns — exportable to S3 or to your SIEM via webhook. We'll include an example trace schema.
20:15 Maya: any blockers for the pilot to move to a 2-week elevated load test?
20:23 Priya: just two things: we need the production-like token distribution and a signed NDA for the extended logs ingestion. Jordan, can you confirm you can provide token distribution?
20:34 Jordan: yes, I'll push that to the shared folder by Tuesday. NDA — I'll check with legal and circle back.

23:01 Alex: okay let's go through a quick repro debugging session — Jordan you mentioned an example payload in the doc, can you read it out?
23:11 Jordan: sure it's the sf-113 sample. sending it now in chat.
23:35 (file shared: sf-113.json)
24:00 Priya: reading — I see the model injected a filler phrase before the start token, probably because the prompt left an ambiguous lead-in. small change: ensure the assistant system message ends with a hard terminal instruction: 'Only output JSON between <JSON_START> and <JSON_END>'. that reduces leakage.
24:45 Omar: does that affect embeddings or reranking?
24:53 Priya: no, that's only for generation endpoints. For embeddings/rerank we use separate paths.

27:10 Maya: can we get a quick runbook for handling schema drift in prod? e.g., when customers add a new optional field, how do we roll that out?
27:22 Alex: best practice: version your schema with a minor version, ship a backward-compatible change, deploy parser tolerant to missing keys, and use the Console to monitor failure rate spikes. Redwood can also gate new fields behind feature flags in the Dedicated route.

30:05 Diego: side note — we saw some jitter when we tested quantized variants. quantization helps cost but sometimes increases tokenization edge cases. avoid mixing quantized and non-quantized in the same rollout cohort.

32:40 Jordan: any known differences between hosted and dedicated for strict-mode behavior?
32:46 Priya: functionally identical; dedicated gives you narrower model selection control and p95 isolation. Hosted uses the same decoding code path. Any behavior difference is usually due to using different model variants or different temperature defaults.

35:00 Alex: recap: Redwood action items — share sample repo + strict-mode example, provide batching/kv config recommendations, and security pack including KMS and audit log examples. Customer action items — run benchmark, share token distribution, and check NDA.
35:25 Jordan: agreed.
35:30 Maya: let's tentatively schedule the security deep-dive for week of Oct 20th.
35:36 Omar: fine by me.

42:15 Priya: last quick note — if you want deterministic JSON, add the post-processor that canonicalizes keys and digits; we have a small lib we can share.
42:28 Jordan: that would be great.
42:35 Alex: okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the repo and docs. meeting adjourned.

Action items (auto): Alex — sample repo; Priya — batching config + lib; Jordan — token distribution & run benchmark; Omar — confirm KMS reqs.

End of transcript.
